title: EFC — Grid-Higgs Framework
description: Introduces the Grid-Higgs Framework, which models spacetime as a dynamic grid whose structural nodes are Higgs-field excitations. In this entropic, energy-flow-based theory, dark matter effects arise from grid tension driven by entropy gradients and black holes are grid-collapse regions; the framework yields testable predictions for lensing, CMB high-ℓ spectra, and gravitational-wave propagation.

energy_flow.description: Energy flow through the spacetime grid is a function of normalized entropy S (0 ≤ S ≤ 1), Higgs node density ρ_H, and a coupling k_k; higher node density and entropy structure regulate flow.

effective_dm_from_entropy_gradient.description: Apparent dark matter arises as an effective density sourced by entropic stress in the grid; λ∇S encodes network tension due to entropy gradients between Higgs nodes.

variable_c.description: The effective speed of light varies with entropy S via a dimensionless function g(S), leading to deviations near strong-entropy-gradient regions (e.g., near event horizons).

dynamic_gravitational_constant.description: The gravitational coupling emerges entropically and varies with entropy through a modulation factor α(S), reducing to Newton’s constant G_N in appropriate limits.

cmb_high_ell_deviation.description: Predicted 7–10% deviation in CMB temperature/polarization power at high multipoles due to entropy damping in the grid.

bh_entropy.description: Grid-collapse regions reproduce the Bekenstein–Hawking area law for black hole entropy in simulations, linking grid failure to black hole thermodynamics.

gw_speed_constraint.description: Gravitational-wave speeds match c to better than 10^-15 where entropy gradients are modest; deviations are expected only in high-entropy environments.

key_results.main_finding: An entropic, Higgs-anchored spacetime grid can reproduce dark-matter-like lensing and galaxy rotation curves and reinterpret black holes as grid-collapse points, with specific, testable entropy-dependent signatures in CMB and gravitational-wave observables.

sealed_predictions.statement: CMB power spectra exhibit a 7–10% suppression/enhancement at multipoles ℓ > 1000 relative to ΛCDM due to entropy damping in the grid.
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: High-ℓ measurements from Planck reanalysis, ACT, SPT, or CMB-S4 that constrain |ΔCℓ/Cℓ| at ℓ > 1000 to <3% with systematics controlled.

sealed_predictions.statement: Weak/strong lensing amplitudes anti-correlate with local entropy S: lensing is enhanced in low-entropy clusters and reduced in high-entropy voids per G_grid(S).
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: Tomographic lensing maps from JWST, Euclid, and LSST showing no statistically significant correlation between inferred convergence and entropy proxies.

sealed_predictions.statement: Gravitational-wave propagation speed deviates from c in high-entropy environments while remaining |Δc_g/c| < 10^-15 in moderate-entropy regions.
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: Multi-messenger GW events or GW lensing/time-delay measurements near dense environments showing no entropy-dependent deviation at the predicted level.

sealed_predictions.statement: Galaxy rotation curves can be matched without particle dark matter, with shapes correlating with spatial variations in ρ_H and ∇S rather than NFW-like halo parameters.
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: Comprehensive rotation-curve samples (e.g., JWST/HST kinematics) demonstrating no correlation between curve shape and entropy/Higgs-node proxies while requiring standard CDM halos.

sealed_predictions.statement: Mass–light separation in merging clusters (e.g., Bullet Cluster analogs) follows the entropic tension term λ∇S rather than collisionless particle offsets.
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: Joint X-ray/SZ/lensing reconstructions where entropy-gradient maps fail to predict lensing-mass peaks and offsets across multiple mergers.

kill_criteria: KC1: High-precision CMB measurements at ℓ > 1000 find |ΔCℓ/Cℓ| ≤ 3% with systematics controlled, inconsistent with the predicted 7–10% entropy-damping signature.
KC2: Multi-messenger gravitational-wave events in demonstrably high-entropy environments show |Δc_g/c| < 10^-15 with no environment-dependent trend.
KC3: Lensing convergence maps across clusters and voids show no statistically significant correlation with entropy proxies, contradicting G_grid(S) dependence.

KC4: Robust detection of a cold, collisionless dark-matter particle with abundance and interaction properties that uniquely explain rotation curves, lensing, and cluster dynamics without entropic-tension terms.
KC5: Event-horizon-scale observations (e.g., EHT) and time-delay measurements show no measurable deviations from constant c or GR predictions attributable to entropy dependence near horizons.
KC6: Numerical grid-collapse models fail to reproduce the Bekenstein–Hawking area law across parameter space, contradicting the claimed black-hole correspondence.
